title: Modal focus effect re-runs on every parent re-render (unstable onClose/extraCloseKeys deps), yanking focus out of the modal and corrupting focus restoration
description: The mount/focus effect depends on [onClose, extraCloseKeys]. All three call sites in App.tsx pass a fresh arrow for onClose (App.tsx:733 KeyboardShortcuts, :738 SubmodelDialog, :749 RenameDialog), and KeyboardShortcuts additionally passes a fresh extraCloseKeys={["?"]} array literal (KeyboardShortcuts.tsx:21). Because App subscribes to frequently-changing store slices (notably hoveredNodeId at App.tsx:156, which updates on every node hover, plus syncBanner/dirty/etc.), App re-renders continuously while a modal is open. Each re-render gives ModalShell new dep references, so the effect's cleanup+setup fire every time: the cleanup runs `previousFocusRef.current.focus()` (pulls focus back to the pre-modal background element), then the setup overwrites `previousFocusRef.current = document.activeElement` and calls `containerRef.current?.focus()` (yanks focus to the modal container). Net effect: while the user hovers nodes in the background graph, the open modal repeatedly steals focus back to its container, so the user cannot keep keyboard focus on an inner control (e.g. Tab-navigating the shortcuts list or typing in RenameDialog's textarea is interrupted), and the saved restore target is repeatedly reset.
evidence: ModalShell.tsx:36 `previousFocusRef.current = document.activeElement`; :37 `containerRef.current?.focus()`; :91-97 cleanup removes listener and `if (previousFocusRef.current instanceof HTMLElement) previousFocusRef.current.focus()`; :98 deps `[onClose, extraCloseKeys]`. App.tsx:733 `onClose={() => setShortcutsOpen(false)}` (new fn each render); KeyboardShortcuts.tsx:21 `extraCloseKeys={["?"]}` (new array each render); App.tsx:156 `const hoveredNodeId = useUIStore((s) => s.hoveredNodeId)` makes App re-render on every hover. No test exercises a parent re-render with changed props (ModalShell.test.tsx / focusTrap / shell-merge all render directly with stable vi.fn() onClose and no extraCloseKeys), so this is uncovered.
